title: WireCat Desktop — main screen
question: Three layouts for the tool manager, all in the WireCat brand. Lock the one to build, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Patch rack
options.lineage: studio equipment racks and patch bays
options.thesis: Each tool is a module in one rack: a status lamp, its version and one action, wired to the machine's power strip at the top.
options.viewport: Thin left rail (Tools, later sections); top strip with OS · Node · npm lamps; six full-width module rows, each opening inline to show details, profiles and the install log.
options.risk: Inline expansion can push other tools off screen when two are open.

options.label: List and detail
options.thesis: A quiet list of tools on the left; the selected tool owns a large detail pane with its action, status and log.
options.viewport: Left: section rail plus a tool list with lamps and versions, readiness at the bottom. Right: the selected tool's name in Unbounded, its install button, requirements, profiles, links and log.
options.risk: The overview of all six tools is narrower; first-time users see one tool's detail before the whole set.

options.label: Command first
options.thesis: One search field leads; tools and actions are results you run with the keyboard, the CLI's grammar given a window.
options.viewport: A wide field reading 'Install, update or check a tool…' above grouped results: Ready, Not installed, Needs attention; a readiness line below; detail opens as a panel on Enter.
options.risk: First-time users who are not keyboard people may not see that the list is clickable.
